bad: "through spring and summer" was read as an interval, giving the producing a start in spring and an end in summer and so asserting a bounded run your sentence never states; "through" has no licensed carrier and a coordinated time frame cannot be split inside one clause. Give each season its own sentence with "in", the form that parsed cleanly for "in deep winter": "In spring the Hollows lanterns produce a steady thread harvest. In summer the Hollows lanterns produce a steady thread harvest." The continuous-span sense of "through" cannot be kept in any wording, but nothing false is asserted.
good. the count, the group, the group-level tending and the per-lantern-keeper distribution all come out, and "the Hollows" stays a plain named individual.
